output.title: Positioning drift starts where the workflow and message diverge
output.body:
Positioning drift usually starts in one place: the gap between what you say you do and what you actually deliver.

For a small business owner, that is not a branding mystery. It is a workflow question. Check the places a customer can see your offer: your website, proposal, email signature, and sales conversation. If those places describe a different service, a different scope, or a different price from the one you actually sell, the drift is already visible.

The practical next step is simple: review your last five proposals, invoices, or customer conversations against your current website wording. Look for one mismatch. Maybe the site still promises support you no longer include. Maybe the proposal template describes a process you stopped using. Maybe your email signature sends a different signal again.

If you find a mismatch, decide which human-owned fix is right: update the message, or change the delivery so it matches the message. That choice stays with you.

If you plan to automate a workflow later, fix this first. Automation will reinforce whatever the offer says today, even if the wording is still stale. A tidy system is less persuasive than a truthful one, but it is easier to work with.
